subject: Missed lab and a makeup plan
scenario: You missed yesterday's biology lab because a clinic visit ran long. Write to your professor.
bullets: Explain why you missed the lab.
Ask for the worksheet or slides.
Propose a time to review the experiment.

subject: Name correction on my record
scenario: Your student record shows a misspelled family name. Write to the registrar.
bullets: State the incorrect spelling and the correct one.
Mention the document that proves the spelling.
Ask how long the change will take.

subject: Swapping our presentation dates
scenario: You and Sam present in the same seminar. You need his Friday slot because of a job interview. Write to Sam.
bullets: Explain the interview conflict.
Ask to trade presentation dates.
Offer to take his original date.

subject: Idea for next month's screening
scenario: You are a member of the film club. Suggest a screening and a short discussion afterward.
bullets: Name the film and why it fits the club.
Propose a date and a room.
Ask what help the organizers need.

subject: Hold that expired while I was away
scenario: A book you reserved was returned to the shelf while you were off campus. Write to the library.
bullets: Give the title of the book.
Explain that you were away when the hold expired.
Ask whether the library can place a new hold.

subject: Heat problem in apartment 4B
scenario: You rent a room near campus. The heater has been out for three days. Write to the manager.
bullets: Describe the heating problem and how long it has lasted.
Explain how it affects your study and sleep.
Request a repair visit and give times you are home.

subject: Question about the essay prompt
scenario: The history essay prompt is unclear about which sources are allowed. Write to the professor.
bullets: Quote or paraphrase the part of the prompt that confuses you.
Ask whether news articles may be used.
Request an example of an acceptable source.

subject: Request to change rooms
scenario: Your room faces a loading dock and the noise starts at dawn. Write to housing.
bullets: Describe the noise and when it happens.
Explain the effect on your classes.
Ask what rooms are available next month.

subject: Cannot host this week's meeting
scenario: You promised to host the debate club, but your residence has a fire drill that evening. Write to the secretary.
bullets: Apologize for canceling the hosting plan.
Explain the fire drill.
Suggest another member's room or a campus lounge.

subject: Recommendation request
scenario: You want to apply for a research assistant post. Ask a professor who knows your lab work.
bullets: Remind the professor which course you took.
Explain the assistant post and the deadline.
Ask if she can write the recommendation.

subject: Question about the guest policy
scenario: Your lease is unclear about family visits. Your parents will be in town for three nights. Write to the landlord.
bullets: State the dates of the visit.
Ask whether three nights are allowed.
Offer to send their names in advance.

subject: Confirming our grammar session
scenario: Jordan offered to review your draft. Confirm the plan and send one question ahead of time.
bullets: Confirm the day and place.
Name the section of the draft you want to review.
Ask Jordan to bring a printed copy if possible.

subject: Need an earlier appointment
scenario: Your checkup is in three weeks, but a form is due sooner. Write to the clinic.
bullets: Explain which form is due.
Ask for an earlier appointment.
Give two mornings when you are free.

subject: Group member has stopped replying
scenario: One person in your project group has not answered messages for a week. Write to the professor.
bullets: Name the project and the problem.
Describe what the group has already finished.
Ask how the grade should be divided if the silence continues.

subject: Wrong edition was sold to me
scenario: You bought a sociology textbook, but the course requires the newer edition. Write to the bookstore.
bullets: Give the course and the edition you received.
Explain that the professor requires the newer edition.
Ask about an exchange or a refund.

subject: Borrowing a camera for a class
scenario: Your visual studies class needs night photos. Ask the club if you may borrow a camera.
bullets: Explain the class assignment.
State the days you need the camera.
Promise to return it in the same condition.

subject: Planning a lighter spring term
scenario: You want to drop one course next term to care for a family responsibility. Write to your advisor.
bullets: Name the course you hope to postpone.
Explain the family responsibility briefly.
Ask whether postponing it delays graduation.

subject: Card charged twice
scenario: The laundry card reader charged you twice for one wash. Write to the service desk.
bullets: Give the date, time, and machine number.
Explain that you paid twice for one cycle.
Ask for a refund on the card.

subject: Arriving late to the midterm
scenario: A delayed train will make you about twenty minutes late for the midterm. Write before the exam.
bullets: Explain the train delay.
Ask whether you may start late.
Ask how much time you will still have.

subject: Changing this week's meeting
scenario: You practice Portuguese and Mandarin with Mei. You have a lab that conflicts this week. Write to Mei.
bullets: Apologize for the conflict.
Explain the lab time.
Offer two other times this week.

subject: Extension for the field report
scenario: Rain canceled your soil samples for a geography field report due Monday. Write to the professor.
bullets: Explain why the samples could not be collected.
Ask for a three-day extension.
Describe what you can submit on the original date.

subject: Cannot open the course files
scenario: The files for your statistics course will not open on your laptop. Write to the help desk.
bullets: Name the course and the error message.
Say what you already tried.
Ask for an appointment or a remote session.
